[LGRA.9.8.4] **Let purity tiers.** Every expression that may appear
in a `let` RHS belongs to one of two tiers
distinguishing its evaluation cost / observability:

- **Pure** — slot access, arithmetic, comparison,
  logical operators, Json introspection (`len`, `has`).
  Inlined at every reference site at compile time;
  no runtime artefact corresponds to the `let`.
- **Sync-impure** — `now()`, `monotonic_ns()` and
  `cached(key)`. Bound once per rule activation at the
  start of the RHS so subsequent references see the same
  value; cheap to evaluate (no I/O), but the bind-once
  semantics are author-visible.

The tier of a let's expression determines the lowering
strategy. Pure expressions inline; sync-impure expressions
are bound once at RHS entry and referenced at use sites.

A construct in the action block
that decides whether the rule fires, and how often, belongs
on the left-hand side where the pattern and its `no` twin
are written openly.
